description:
ExecutableEffects(E) and CallableConstruction(position) become engine derivations whose group concludes together. Deletes pull.rs pending_strong_component (16,005 calls on the distiller, 651 closed searches over 389 distinct pairs, groups up to 101), the pending-record cycle evidence, and with it the 168 missed cycles (records dropped by settle Wake 123 / Invalidate 39 / both 6). Predict: dumps identical; missed cycles 0.

Spiked 2026-11-14 on e47d83e40 (scratchpad t93_4/findings.md, spike.diff, tests_spike.log; ExecutableEffects only): dumps and outputs identical, but +1.0% distiller instructions (12.44G -> 12.58G, n=5) and +3,345 DeriveExecutableEffects jobs. An engine job's product wait on a same-root product deadlocks today's driver: the active drive's scope parks the request until the drive ends, the drive waits on the job. The spike needed a take_parked nested-drive bridge (1,103 extra drives) and still failed macro_product_test ('runtime demand with no ready producer') and a public_trace scenario ('product movement outside a session'). Premise correction: pending_strong_component's calls and missed cycles are mostly Reach (8,776 calls, 155 of 155 missed cycles after ExecutableEffects moves; CallableConstruction 3,471 calls, 0 missed). So this step cannot delete pending_strong_component alone. Reordered AFTER fz-t93.7: once Materialized is a derivation, the wait is an ordinary fact wait and needs no bridge.

FOLDED into fz-t93.7 (2026-11-14, user-approved plan /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-next.html): its products convert bottom-up within the pull deletion, which removes the same-root product-wait deadlock it hit.
title: Recursive product groups are engine derivations
